messages:
Sofia L.: Heads up — seeing a weird 'pocketing' pattern on local SSDs in us-west1. A subset of drives are taking all the write bursts and queue depth spikes, GPU attach latency climbed to ~45s and about ~30% launch failures in the last hour.
Akshay: which gnode/fleet/rack? paste iostat/nvme top when you have a sec.
Sofia L.: gnode-cc-rack3 (3 nodes). iostat snapshot (trimmed):
```
Device:         tps    kB_read/s    kB_wrtn/s
nvme0n1       8200       0.0        65000.0
nvme1n1         12     100.0           0.0
nvme2n1         10      90.0           0.0
```
Pattern repeats every ~30s — huge write bursts on nvme0n1 only.
Jem: that matches janitor/cleaner coalescing where GC windows hit the same namespace -> "pocketing". Did a scrub or deep-clean run overlap with the batch GPU window?
Sofia L.: yes — scrub cron kicked at 02:05 UTC, same time as a batch scale-up. scrub throughput peaked and pinned the driver queues.
Akshay: short-term mitigation: lower scrub/janitor concurrency for that pool and throttle cleaner I/O. Proposed change: set JANITOR_CONCURRENCY=2 for us-west1 scrub cron and add --io-rate=50MB/s to cleaner on rack3. Canary to one rack first.
Sofia L.: good. canary target should be rack3 only. also we should set attach fallback to local-ssd-fallback pool for 10m to avoid launch failures.
infra-bot: deployment triggered: scrub-config-rollout -> canary to rack3 (job id: deploy-7742).
Marco: long-term we should smooth janitor scheduling (stagger windows) and add write spreading so cleans don't concentrate. Also consider background rewrite throttles and per-namespace pacing.
Jem: note cost tradeoff: falling back to a reserved ephemeral pool reduces failures but increases reserved capacity cost. Cross-region reschedule would add egress. Need to quantify.
Sofia L.: Plan posted here: 1) Canary scrub concurrency -> 2 on rack3, 2) Add cleaner io-rate throttle, 3) Temporary attach fallback enabled for 10m, 4) Monitor for 2h and rollback if attach-fail-rate > 5% or gpu-launch-latency worsens.
Akshay: pushing canary now, tagging @oncall. I'll also add a short-term Grafana panel for per-node nvme queue depth.
Sofia L.: added KPIs to monitor: gpu-launch-latency, attach-fail-rate, avg-nvme-queue-depth, scrub-throughput.
Marco: add an alert: avg queue depth > 100 for >5m => automatic throttle of scrubers and notify infra-oncall.
Sofia L.: putting that into the runbook. executing canary rollout in 2m. :thumbsup:
Akshay: canary started. initial telemetry already shows queue depth flattening on the canary node.
Sofia L.: nice. will keep thread updated with metrics. if stable after 30m we should roll to other racks with spaced windows.
Akshay: noted. if we see any nvme SMART spikes we will abort and revert.
Sofia L.: thanks all — updating incident log and runbook with mitigation steps.
